sections.label: GST on low-value goods
sections.summary: Amendments introduce GST for low-value goods imported via air or post and for B2C imported non-digital services from 1 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To close this gap, the first set of amendments introduces GST for goods that are valued up to the current GST import relief threshold of $400, or "low-value goods", that are imported via air or post from 1 January 2023 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments also introduces GST for business-to-consumer, or B2C, imported non-digital services, such as live interaction with overseas providers of educational learning and telemedicine.

sections.label: GST treatment of media sales
sections.summary: From 1 January 2022, GST treatment of media sales will be based on where the contracting person and the benefiting person belong.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We, therefore, need to update and revise the GST treatment of media sales.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Thus, with effect from 1 January 2022, the GST treatment for the supply of media sales will instead be based on where the person who contracts for the service, for example, a local or overseas headquarters or HQ, and the person who directly benefits from the service, for example, a subsidiary in Singapore, belong.

sections.label: Updated GST transitional rules
sections.summary: Updated transitional rules apply to GST treatment changes from 1 January 2022, covering imported services, clarifying elections and making administrative changes under clauses 16, 4 to 6 and 25.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The proposed updated transitional rules will help prevent revenue risks, particularly for related-party transactions, provide tax certainty and ease the compliance burden of taxpayers whenever there is a change in GST treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These proposed updated transitional rules will apply to changes, such as the proposed change of GST treatment for a supply of media sales, from 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This amendment updates the transitional rules, such as to cover imported services, clarifies the application of elections under the transitional rules and makes various administrative changes that are necessary for a smooth transition of a new GST treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 16 of the Bill provides for these amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These are regimes for enforcing GST on low-value goods imported via air or post and imported services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The miscellaneous changes seek to prevent revenue risks, provide tax certainty and ease the compliance burden.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These miscellaneous changes are found in clauses 4 to 6 and 25 of the Bill.

sections.label: Businesses welcome GST on imports
sections.summary: The Government's move to apply GST to lower-value overseas imports via air is highly anticipated and welcomed by local businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government’s move to apply GST to lower-value overseas imports via air is highly anticipated and welcomed by the local businesses that I have spoken with.

sections.label: Implementation with foreign merchants
sections.summary: A question asks how the policy will be implemented given the number of independent foreign merchants offering direct shipping to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the sheer number of independent foreign merchants that offer direct shipping to Singapore, how will this policy be implemented?

sections.label: Impact on lower-income households
sections.summary: Besides administrative issues, the tax on lower-cost goods affecting lower-income households is another cause for concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Besides administrative issues, the fact that this tax on lower-cost goods would affect lower-income households is another cause for concern.

sections.label: Policy impact on inflation
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to share data on how the policy may affect overall inflation and living costs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share data on how this policy may impact overall inflation and living costs in Singapore, even at the margin, especially so given the already inherent pressures and delays from supply chain disruption risks?

sections.label: Online sales and retail vacancy
sections.summary: Online sales were 16.4% of total retail sales excluding motor vehicles in August, with retail space vacancy at 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fast forward to this year, these points continue to be relevant, with online sales now representing 16.4% of total retail sales, excluding motor vehicles, in August this year and with vacancy rates of retail space remaining elevated at 8% despite declining retail rents since 2015, given the challenges faced by the retail industry and made worse by multiple waves of COVID-19-related restrictions.

sections.label: Netflix tax revenue estimate
sections.summary: In November 2018, the House was told the Government expects about $90 million per year from the so-called Netflix tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In November 2018, it was shared in this House that the Government expects additional revenue of about $90 million per year from this so-called "Netflix tax".

sections.label: GST on imported goods
sections.summary: From 1 January 2023, GST will apply to goods imported by air or post up to S$400 and imported non-digital services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, I understand that from 1 January 2023, GST will now apply to goods imported by air or post with a value of up to S$400, as well as imported non-digital services.

sections.label: GST receipts from low-value goods
sections.summary: The Government is asked how much GST it expects to collect from low-value goods and imported non-digital services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I recognise that this new Bill is also about protecting Singapore's revenue base, not just merely about the additional GST receipts from the imposition of GST on these categories of goods and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But how much does the Government expect to collect in GST receipts from each of the low-value goods and imported non-digital services?

sections.label: GST import relief and hike
sections.summary: The passage asks if the $500 GST import relief stays, and notes the planned GST hike from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, travellers are granted GST import relief on new goods that are purchased overseas and brought into Singapore for their personal use, with the relief amount set at $500 with 48 hours spent away from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister if this GST relief is expected to stay intact even when GST on low-value goods is in place from 2023?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is on the spectre of a looming GST hike from 7% to 9% amid current macroeconomic uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To which, Minister Lawrence Wong responded that, "The Government has announced that the GST rate increase will take place sometime during 2022 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This remains unchanged and we will continue to consider all factors, including our fiscal needs as well as the prevailing economic conditions in deciding on the timing of the GST rate increase." While I agree with the need to roll out GST on low-value goods and imported non-digital services, the target implementation from 1 January 2023, coupled with the "sooner rather than later" hike in GST rates, could mean a double whammy for consumers.

sections.label: Singapore online sales growth
sections.summary: Online sales in Singapore are estimated at US$8 billion this year and expected to reach US$10 billion by end-2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Online sales in Singapore will hit an estimated US$8 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent report by Bain & Company, e-commerce sales in Singapore are expected to grow to US$10 billion by the end of 2026.

sections.label: Pasir Ris merchants' falling business
sections.summary: Pasir Ris merchants selling low-value household items said their business fell by up to 40% to 50% since the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In my recent discussion with our Merchants Association in Pasir Ris, our merchants, especially those that sell low-value household items, such as hardware, tools, curtains, small pieces of furniture and non-perishable products, shared that since the pandemic, their business has gone down by up to 40% to 50%.

sections.label: GST income for retailer support
sections.summary: An MP asks whether GST income from low-value overseas items could fund support for neighbourhood retailers' digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since the intent of introducing GST to low-value items from overseas is to level the playing field, can the Ministry consider the tax income from the activity to be used to provide more support for our neighbourhood retailers, such as hiring more consultants or trainers, to guide more retailers through their digital transformation and provide a support package for the small retailers to continue to sustain their digital activities?

sections.label: GST on low-value imports
sections.summary: GST on imports of low-value goods below $400 aims to make local consumers buy from local suppliers instead of abroad.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The imposition of GST on imports of low-value goods below $400 seeks to address this problem, in hopes that local consumers channel their purchases to local suppliers rather than those abroad.

sections.label: GST impact on local businesses
sections.summary: GST on low-value goods imports may dent profit margins of local businesses like Jia Jia's that source mainly from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I remember I myself even hosted a “Passions to Profit – Mumpreneur” Home Baking Class with my colleagues from the NTUC Learning Hub and over 300 Mumpreneurs have signed up for the classes since then.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, because of the GST imposed on the import of low-value goods, local businesses like Jia Jia’s might face a significant dent in their profit margins, especially if they source mainly from overseas.

sections.label: Unrecognised businesses' lack of support
sections.summary: Businesses lacking recognition in the formal economy get no equipment subsidies and face restrictions, struggling to compete.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Due to their lack of recognition in the formal economy, these businesses do not receive subsidies for equipment and, sometimes, have restrictions on who they can even do business with, with or without a licence, leading them to struggle to even compete with some of their larger SME counterparts, much less overseas competitors.

sections.label: Level playing field for businesses
sections.summary: The passage asks whether efforts to level the playing field have made things harder for some businesses meant to be supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In our bid to level the playing field, have we inadvertently made the hill a little bit steeper for some businesses we had intended to support?

sections.label: Pazzion store and café
sections.summary: Pazzion opened its first store in Marina Square in 2005, had its 10th local outlet by 2019, expanded in Asia Pacific, and opened a café at Jewel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Pazzion opened its first brick-and-mortar store in Marina Square in 2005 and boasts its 10th local outlet as of 2019, in the meantime building its presence in Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is interesting about Pazzion, however, is that, in recent years, it has broken out of its mould as a fashion business and opened a café over at Jewel, committing to becoming a lifestyle brand that sells experiences beyond goods.

sections.label: GST changes and retail support
sections.summary: The passage calls for distinguishing microbusinesses and home-based businesses on GST changes, asks agencies to revitalise retail, and notes the Bill extends GST to imported low-value goods and updates media sales treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With this, I call for the distinction to be made for microbusinesses, especially our home-based businesses, when it comes to GST changes and other provisions for growth support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Further, I call on Government agencies to think bigger in revitalising Singaporean retail, going beyond propping up businesses in the short term, to architect a real retail environment for the ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Significantly, this Bill will extend GST to imported low-value goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill will also update the GST treatment for media sales to more closely reflect the reality of how services are advertised and consumed.

sections.label: Media sales GST treatment
sections.summary: Amendments to section 21 make GST treatment for media sales depend on where the customer and direct beneficiary belong, not where the advertisement is circulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments to section 21 mean that the GST treatment for supplies of media sales depends on where the customer and the direct beneficiary of the service belongs, rather than where the advertisement is circulated.

sections.label: Best available information for goods
sections.summary: New section 14(1B) lets a recipient rely on best available information to determine if goods are distantly taxable when unable to verify location or transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 14(1B) provides that a recipient may rely on the best available information to determine whether goods are distantly taxable if the recipient is unable to verify the location of the goods at the point of sale of the goods or how the goods will be transported to a place in the customs territory.

sections.label: Taxing imports by air or post
sections.summary: The passage says the general term best available information may pose enforcement issues, projects $8 billion in 2025, and states taxing all imports by air or post will help level the playing field for local retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This clarification is important because the term “best available information” is so general that it might pose enforcement issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is projected to reach $8 billion in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The decision to impose taxes on all imports by air or post will help to level the playing field for our local retailers.

sections.label: Lower cost of foreign goods
sections.summary: A survey found eight in 10 local respondents said the main reason was the overall lower cost of procuring goods and services from foreign sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to a survey, eight in 10 local respondents shared that the main reason was the overall lower cost of procuring goods and services from foreign sites.

sections.label: Tax collection under international agreements
sections.summary: Under international agreements, it can ask counterparts in some countries to collect tax or pursue unpaid tax through a retailer's national courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under international agreements, it can request counterparts in some countries to collect tax on its behalf or assess and pursue unpaid tax through a retailer’s national courts.

sections.label: SingPost online GST collection system
sections.summary: SingPost switched to an online cashless system for collecting GST on packages above $400, and more packages will be due for GST payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SingPost has recently switched to an online cashless system for collecting GST on packages valued above $400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new policy would see a significant rise in the number of packages due for GST payment.

sections.label: Tracking parcels and GST payment
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government will keep track of all parcels entering Singapore and their GST payment status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Government keep track of all parcels coming into Singapore and their GST payment status?

sections.label: Support for lower-income groups
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to support lower-income groups, micro businesses and entrepreneurs like Mdm K who may be significantly affected if the tax is passed to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And Mdm K brings in items in small amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge the Government to provide some support to the lower-income groups, micro businesses and entrepreneurs like Mdm K and her family who may be significantly affected by the changes, if the tax is passed to them.

sections.label: Enforcement resources for lower-value GST
sections.summary: One concern of levying GST on lower-value items is whether the resources required to enforce collection are worth the effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the concerns of levying GST on lower-value items is whether the resources required to enforce the collection are worth the effort.

sections.label: Simplified registration for foreign suppliers
sections.summary: IRAS should implement a simplified registration and compliance regime to facilitate tax compliance for foreign online suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To facilitate tax compliance for foreign online suppliers, IRAS should implement a simplified registration and compliance regime.

sections.label: Australia GST revenue figures
sections.summary: Australia recorded over AUD 1 billion of GST collected in the first two years for online services and digital products and first year for goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, Australia recorded total revenues of over AUD 1 billion of GST collected in the first two years of operating its GST regime for online sales of services and digital products and in the first year of its implementation for online sales of goods.

sections.label: Earmarking tax revenue for retail
sections.summary: It asks whether a portion of tax revenue from imported purchases can be earmarked to strengthen retail sector resilience in a major economic downturn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can a portion of tax revenue collected from these imported purchases be earmarked to strengthen the resilience of our retail sector in the event it encounters another major economic downturn like now?

sections.label: Widening OVR and RC regimes
sections.summary: GST on low-value goods imported by air or post and B2C imported non-digital services will be implemented by widening the OVR and RC regimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: GST on low-value goods imported via air or post and B2C imported non-digital services will be implemented by widening the scope of our existing Overseas Vendor Registration, or OVR, and Reverse Charge, or RC regimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the OVR regime, overseas vendors, such as overseas suppliers, electronic marketplace operators and re-deliverers that make significant B2C supplies of imported services and/or low-value goods imported by air or post to non-GST registered customers in Singapore will register with IRAS if they are not already registered.

sections.label: Reverse Charge for B2B imports
sections.summary: Under the RC regime, applicable only to B2B transactions, local GST-registered entities account for GST to IRAS on imported low-value goods and B2B services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the RC regime, which is only applicable to B2B transactions, local GST-registered entities will account for GST to IRAS when they import low-value goods via air or post or buy B2B services from overseas suppliers.

sections.label: Exemption thresholds for GST registration
sections.summary: Businesses with annual turnover under $1 million and not importing services exceeding $1 million need not register for GST or apply RC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Businesses with annual turnover of less than $1 million and not importing services exceeding $1 million are not required to register for GST and are not required to apply RC on their imported services.

sections.label: Overseas vendor digital services regime
sections.summary: Since 1 January 2020, the regime applies to overseas vendors selling B2C digital services to local consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, since 1 January 2020, the regime is already in place for overseas vendors that sell B2C digital services to local consumers.

sections.label: Media sales GST treatment revision
sections.summary: From 1 January 2022, GST treatment for media sales suppliers is based on where the contracting person and direct beneficiary belong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To recap, the GST treatment for a supplier of media sales will be revised from 1 January 2022, to be based on where the person who contracts for the service, for example, a local or overseas headquarters, and the person who directly benefits from the service, for example, a subsidiary in Singapore, belong.

sections.label: Conditions for sole direct beneficiary
sections.summary: Both conditions must be satisfied for the contractual client to be regarded as the sole direct beneficiary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To clarify, both conditions must be satisfied for the contractual client to be regarded as the sole direct beneficiary.

sections.label: Overseas headquarters subsidiary example
sections.summary: If the contract is with an overseas headquarters but media sales go to a Singapore subsidiary, that subsidiary is the direct beneficiary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For example, if the media sales supplier's contract is with an overseas headquarters, but the contract requires the media sales to be, first, provided to a subsidiary in Singapore, or second, the media sales supplier is accountable to the subsidiary in Singapore for his service deliverables, then the subsidiary in Singapore is the direct beneficiary of the service.

sections.label: GST extension to imported goods
sections.summary: From 1 January 2023, GST extends to low-value goods imported via air or post and imported B2C non-digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With the extension of GST to low-value goods imported via air or post and to imported B2C non-digital services from 1 January 2023 as announced in Budget 2021, this means that GST will apply to goods and services imported into Singapore.

sections.label: Revenue and transformation support
sections.summary: Revenue collected forms part of total fiscal resources, with $24 billion set aside over three years to help firms and workers transform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The revenue collected will form part of our total fiscal resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have set aside $24 billion over the next three years, as announced in Budget 2021, to enable firms and workers to transform and emerge stronger from the pandemic, of which a key focus is to support SMEs in their digitial adoption.

sections.label: GST from OVR and RC regimes
sections.summary: The GST collection from existing OVR and RC regimes is about $250 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: He had asked for the GST collection from our existing OVR and RC regimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the answer to that is that it is about $250 million a year.

sections.label: Yield of the measures
sections.summary: The measures would yield about $130 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The measures would yield about $130 million a year.

sections.label: Land sales as revenue
sections.summary: The suggestion is to treat land sales as revenue, which is not done because selling does not make you richer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But in a nutshell, what they are really saying is, if you have land, if you have property, today, it is in the physical form; when you sell it, you are converting it to cash, to another form – and the suggestion is to treat that as revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We do not treat it as revenue because you have not become richer by selling it.

sections.label: Net GST from higher-income and foreigners
sections.summary: Over 60% of net GST from households and individuals is estimated to come from higher-income people, foreigners and tourists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In terms of GST, as I mentioned yesterday, over 60% of the net GST from households and individuals is estimated to be from the higher-income and from the foreigners who live and work in Singapore and from tourists.

sections.label: Five Budgets during pandemic
sections.summary: During the pandemic, there were five Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: When you consider the pandemic, we had five Budgets.

sections.label: Support for the genuinely needy
sections.summary: The Government will support those in genuine need, which requires diverse sustainable revenue sources and recurrent revenue for recurrent expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The other takeaway is really that this Government will always make sure that whoever is in need, in genuine need, will have support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the only way you can do that is to have diverse revenue sources which are sustainable; and for recurrent expenditure, to make sure that you have recurrent revenue.
